newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 25.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
PARTY UNITY TOPS NEW CONGRESS CHIEF'S AGENDA

Restoring unity in the Congress party tops the agenda of new party chief Sitaram Kesri. Stating this, he said there would be no departure from former party chief P.V. Narasimha Rao's policies. Kesri ruled out the possibility of any change in the party's support to the United Front Government. Forces interested in strengthening the party were always welcome to join the party, Kesri said. But, those wanting to weaken it have to be watched out, he warned.
SELLOFF RULE FOR 100 PCT FOREIGN STAKE IN CONSUMER GOODS

The government may permit foreign companies to set up 100 percent subsidiaries in the consumer goods sector only if they dilute their equity within a stipulated period. The government is also considering extending this guideline to foreign companies which are already in operation in the consumer goods sector and have been given permission to set up fully owned subsidiaries. While the level of dilution has still not worked out, sources said it could be upto 49 percent.
NORMS SOON FOR 100 PCT FOREIGN INVESTMENT

Industry secretary N. Mohanty said the government would soon come out with fresh criteria for 100 percent foreign investments. He revealed this at the government roundtable organised by the Economic Intelligence Unit. Mohanty said such investments would be permitted by a foreign company having propriety technology and an international brand. Permission would also be given in cases where two or more foreign companies come together to invest in the country, he added.
RELIANCE NET EXPECTED TO DIP 26 PCT

Reliance Industries is heading for a steep fall in post tax profit for the six months ended September 30. This was shown by a poll of leading brokerages. Net profit forecasts for Reliance by 14 major securities firms averaged 4.7 billion rupees, 25.8 percent down from the first six months of the previous year. Sales were forecast to fall 21.1 percent to an average 31.3 billion rupees during the period.
KHAITANS MARRY MCLEOD RUSSEL WITH EVEREADY

Williamson Magor Group's Mcleod Russel India Ltd is set to merge with Eveready Industries India Ltd. Williamson Magor acquired Mcleod Russel in November 1994 at a price of over 2.9 billion rupees. The share swap ratio for the amalgamation has been fixed at two shares of Eveready for every three shares of Mcleod Russel. The merger will be effective from April 1, 1996. The merged equity of Eveready Industries will have a networth of about 8.5 billion rupees and a projected turnover of over six billion rupees for the year ended March 1997 and 10 billion rupees over the next three years.

The country is facing an economic slowdown this year in terms of gross domestic product and export and import growth, the Union Commerce secretary has said. So far in 1996-97, export growth had remained at 10 percent as compared to over 20 percent in the last few years, he informed. Import growth, too, had slowed down to 4-4.5 percent this year. The slowdown in import growth rate showed a decline in domestic manufacturing. This had given rise to fears of recession, he added.
ESSAR POWER ALLOWED TO RAISE $100 MLN

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board has cleared Essar Power's proposal to bring in $100 million through Prime Asia Ltd of Netherlands. Essar Power is setting up a 515 MW duel- fuel power plant at Hazira, Gujarat at an estimated cost of 17.66 billion rupees. The total equity component to the project is $175 million. The Indian component of the equity has been bought in by Essar Steel and Essar Oil for 2.57 billion rupees and six billion rupees respectively.
